area: Translation / i18n state of the Solen.ch web app (locale catalogue, language switching, hardcoded copy, DB-side locale columns, CI gates, French register)
summary: The message catalogue is NOT the problem: messages/{de,en,fr,it}.json are 5703 keys each, perfectly in parity, with essentially zero untranslated values (the only en/de-identical long strings are the word "Salon", a Swiss address placeholder, and two ICU plural strings). The problem is everything outside next-intl. (1) Language switching is genuinely broken: the only path-preserving, cookie-setting switcher (components-legacy/ui/LanguageSwitcher.tsx) is mounted in exactly one place, the MobileMenu, whose hamburger trigger is `md:hidden` — so on desktop there is no working switcher at all, only a footer row of `<Link href={`/${code}`}>` that throws you to the target locale's HOMEPAGE and never sets the NEXT_LOCALE cookie. (2) /profile/settings/language lets you pick a language, PATCHes profiles.locale, toasts "saved" and calls router.refresh() — the URL keeps the old locale segment so the UI does not change language at all; it only affects emails. (3) 109 TSX files carry 543 hardcoded German user-facing literals outside /dev/, 27 of those files already call t() (that is literally the "mixed german english" the owner sees), and the shared booking DateTimePicker primitive ships German defaults that the homepage search bar never overrides. (4) The DB is structurally German/English-only for the content that matters: services.name_*, services.description_*, salons.description_*, service_options.name_*, salon_badges.name_* and nail_dynamic_pricing_rules.label_* have de+en and NO fr/it columns, and 12 read sites hard-code `locale === 'en' ? x_en : x_de`, so French and Italian users get German service names everywhere — while app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonServices.tsx:172 renders `{service.name_de}` unconditionally, meaning even English users see German service names on the salon PDP. (5) /terms and /privacy render German AND English paragraphs side by side on all four locales with no French or Italian at all. (6) The i18n CI job is RED right now: check-i18n-sentinel.mjs exits 1 on all four locale files.

Zero empty strings in any locale. Catalogue sizes: de 261,477 B / en 245,044 / fr 269,552 / it 261,646.

findings.claim: `node scripts/check-i18n-sentinel.mjs` FAILS TODAY, exit 1. It reports `[FAIL] messages/<locale>.json has 1 non-string leaf value(s): dashboard.approvalsPage.checklistItems = [...]` for all four locales. The identical-to-en ratchet itself passes at its baselines: de 466 (baseline 466), fr 368 (368), it 220 (220). findings.claim: SILENT NO-OP: /profile/settings/language changes nothing about the UI language. SettingsForm.tsx:376-404 (section==="language") posts through saveProfile (:92-131) which PATCHes /api/profile with `locale: form.locale`, toasts success and calls `router.refresh()`. It never writes the NEXT_LOCALE cookie and never navigates to the new locale prefix, and next-intl resolves the locale from the URL segment, so the page re-renders in the OLD language. The column is genuinely persisted (updateProfileSchema line 157 accepts `locale: z.enum(["de","en","fr","it"])`, /api/profile PATCH writes it) and IS read by ~10 email senders , so the control is email-only. The helper text does say so ("Für E-Mails und Erinnerungen" / "Used for emails and reminders", messages/*.json line 35), but the page is titled "Sprache" and sits in Settings, so it reads as the site-language switch and silently is not one.

findings.claim: Three different, mutually inconsistent language-switch mechanisms coexist: (a) MobileMenu sheet = path swap + cookie, (b) Footer links = jump to locale homepage, no cookie, (c) Settings page = DB write, no UI effect. findings.claim: WHAT THE GATES CHECK AND MISS. check-i18n-parity.mjs: flattens the 4 JSON files and fails if any key is present in one locale and absent in another (hard zero, both directions). It does NOT look at values at all, so a locale file full of German values passes. check-i18n-sentinel.mjs: (a) hard-zero on any non-string leaf, (b) a per-locale ratchet on the count of strings identical to en.json (baselines de 466 / fr 368 / it 220), failing only when the count goes UP. It does NOT detect a value that is translated-but-wrong, a wrong register, or a German string that merely differs from the English one. NEITHER script scans .tsx source, so 100% of the 543 hardcoded German literals and 100% of the inline locale-map files are invisible to both. Wiring: both run in the `i18n` job of .github/workflows/quality.yml (on push to main + every PR). There is NO pre-commit hook (/Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.git/hooks contains only *.sample). package.json exposes `check:i18n-parity` (line 16) but has NO `check:i18n-sentinel` script , the sentinel is only reachable via the CI step or a direct node invocation.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs whole file (flatten + key-set diff, no value comparison); scripts/check-i18n-sentinel.mjs:60-95 (non-string leaves + IDENTICAL_BASELINE ratchet); .github/workflows/quality.yml:162-174; package.json:16 and absence of a sentinel entry in :5-35; `ls /Users/sulo/Documents/solen/.git/hooks` returns 14 *.sample files and nothing else
